Hi Sam / Elena,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clarity on the 2 product lines you want to standardize under a single runtime. I attached a compact tier proposal (FathomAI_Proposed_Tier_Summary.pdf) that attempts to balance:

- a modest up-front commitment (12 months) to unlock an implementation credit,
- a steeper seat/throughput discount as you step up usage buckets, and
- a fallthrough runtime SLA credit for missed latency targets.

Key ask: can you confirm the expected 90-day pilot QPS and the percentage of calls that require latency <150ms? That will let us tighten the seat-to-commitment ratio.

If you want to preserve flexibility we can move to an initial 6-month commitment with lower credits and a migration credit on go-live. Putting both options in the SOW helps legal speed review. I attached a SOW draft (SOW_draft_v2.docx) with placeholders for the pilot KPIs.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Stephanie — thanks for the fast turnaround and thoughtful options. Quick questions from our procurement side before we schedule a follow-up:

1) The pilot QPS will be ~450 QPS, but only ~30% are latency-critical (<150ms).
2) We want the most flexibility on model variants during pilot — can the commitment bucket be scoped to consumed tokens rather than seat tiers (we expect bursty traffic)?
3) On credits: how fungible is the implementation credit across SSO/integration and model-compat testing? Our internal PM wants it to cover engineers + software vendor costs.

Also — pricing leadership here pushes back on anything that looks like a heavy multi-year lock. Is there a bridge structure that gives us equivalent unit economics without committing to 12 months?

If it's easier, loop your commercial lead and ops (cc'd) and we can do a short call.

Best,
Sam Torres
Head of Platform Partnerships, FathomAI
sam.torres@fathomai.com

Dylan / Karthik — forwarding Sam's note (excerpted above). He confirmed 450 QPS and that only ~30% need low-latency. Procurement is pushing back on 12-month locks and wants token-based commitments or a bridge.

My thoughts:
- Option A (our baseline): 12-mo soft-commit with implementation credit ($45k) + stepped per-token discounts at 10M, 50M, 150M token thresholds. Best unit economics for Redwood but requires internal approval for the credit.
- Option B (bridge): 3-mo pilot commit to a minimum consumed token floor (token-bucket) that converts to a 9-month amortized commitment if they exceed X tokens within pilot. Implementation credit reduced to $18k. Gives them runway and preserves upside if they scale.
- Option C (flexible): no time lock, prepay credit pool (smaller) + increased per-token price but with an onboarding rebate if they hit pilot KPIs. Easiest for legal but worst for our revenue predictability.

Attached two sketches: a quick $/token schedule and a draft clause for token-bucket conversion. Need your take on what revenue ops will tolerate and whether we can route the implementation credit as a one-time service credit (not invoice credit) to avoid complex GAAP impact.

Can we decide today so I can get a response to Sam tomorrow?

Thanks,
Steph

Attachments: commercial_sketch_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tiered bundle repack & commitment squeeze — revised options

Sam / Elena — thanks for the clarity. Per internal alignment (cc'd) here are two concrete options for your review. I attached the updated one-pager and a clean SOW link.

Option 1 — Bridge-first (recommended)
- 3-month pilot with a token-bucket minimum of 5M tokens (consumed).
- Implementation credit: $20k applied as service onboarding credit (covers SSO, model-compat testing).
- If pilot consumption > 20M tokens, automatic conversion to a 9-month amortized commitment at the discounted tiers (10% lower unit price than no-commit).
- SLA: standard latency SLO, with 50% credit on missed availability SLAs (pilot-only).

Option 2 — Predictable-commit (aggressive economics)
- 12-month soft-commit with stepped pricing at 10M/50M/150M tokens.
- Implementation credit: $45k (one-time service credit).
- Early-exit clause: 60-day notice with pro-rated buyout equal to remaining discount-weighted consumption.

Comparison notes:
- Option 1 preserves flexibility they asked for (token-bucket) while giving us a path to revenue recognition if adoption accelerates.
- Option 2 gets the best revenue and gives FathomAI the lowest unit price but adds friction on legal.

Next steps: pick an option and confirm any non-standard procurement terms you need (vendor invoice requirements, PO timing). If preferred, we can convert Option 1 into a short term-sheet and do a client call Friday afternoon.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: FathomAI_Revised_OnePager.pdf (pdf, 2 pages), SOW_draft_v2_clean.docx (docx, 5 pages)
